title: Molten Glass Rain on a Blue Planet
hook: What if rain fell sideways at 8,000 kilometres per hour?
script: What if rain fell sideways at 8,000 kilometres per hour? This is HD 189733b, a deep blue world not painted by oceans, but by clouds of silicate. Those clouds create rain that doesn’t fall straight down, but sideways, slicing through the atmosphere. Temperatures here soar to 1,000 degrees Celsius, hot enough to vaporize solid material into liquid glass. The planet spins rapidly, completing a rotation in just 13.1 hours, intensifying this hellish weather. One side of HD 189733b is eternally scorched by its star, while the other remains cloaked in darkness. So, on a planet that can turn solid rock into molten rain, how different is our own weather, really?
